description: Phase 5c gate — kqueue async I/O backend. Drives the disk backend with LEAP_IO_BACKEND=kqueue so that commit durability (atomic-rename + fsync + dir-fsync) runs through the worker-thread pool from io_backend_kqueue, with F_FULLFSYNC on Darwin. Per spec/io-backend-kqueue.spec.md § 'Test authority': every fixture that passes on the sync backend MUST pass byte-identically with the kqueue backend active. This fixture inherits phase3d's step-kind vocabulary and adds no new schema fields; the harness merely forces the env var at run time. The max-invariant case — 1000 INSERTs then reopen + SELECT count — is the async analogue of phase3d's minimal roundtrip and is the observable gate for both targets. Cross-build equivalence between C and Rust is pinned by the expect blocks below.

schema.case: inherits phase3d.json schema. No new fields.
schema.env: Harness sets LEAP_IO_BACKEND=kqueue for every step; the async pager routes commit durability through io_backend_kqueue.

cases.name: disk-async-roundtrip-small
cases.description: Async backend: smallest observable roundtrip — CREATE, INSERT, close, reopen, SELECT. Same pass criterion as phase3d disk-normal-commit-survives-reopen but under the async commit path.

cases.name: disk-async-multiple-commit-cycles
cases.description: Exercises the async commit path across multiple close+reopen cycles. Each reopen must re-read bytes durably flushed via F_FULLFSYNC.

cases.name: disk-async-text-roundtrip
cases.description: TEXT values round-trip cleanly through the async commit path — guards against buffer-lifecycle regressions in the pipelined pwrite path.

cases.name: disk-async-1000-inserts-roundtrip
cases.description: Task-required gate: 1000 INSERTs, reopen, verify all 1000 come back in order. Exercises the async pager's pipelined pwrite path (64 KiB chunks, depth 16) across a buffer that spans multiple worker-queue generations.
